checks: Checked on storms it never saw

parts.d: Radar rain, corrected with gauges, on every 1 km square every hour.
parts.done: Hourly radar rain for every past storm and for every live forecast cycle.
parts.left: Nothing planned.
parts.prob: Hourly steps smooth out short bursts of 5 to 15 minutes.

parts.d: The newest eight NOAA HRRR forecasts, up to 48 hours ahead.
parts.done: Eight forecasts every hour, a rain gate that starts the flood model, and spreading of the forecast rain to allow for misplaced storms.
parts.left: Compare the forecast rain with the radar automatically after every storm.
parts.prob: Forecast rain can be wrong in amount and place, and that carries straight into the road list.

parts.d: Air temperature from the forecast splits rain from snow.
parts.done: Live since 13 Nov 2026.
parts.left: Check it on the first cold-season storm.
parts.prob: No storm cold enough to check it has happened since it went live.

parts.d: USGS lidar, used on a 20 m grid, with streams carved in and road crossings opened.
parts.done: District-wide terrain with carved streams and opened road–stream crossings.
parts.left: Finer squares in dense town centres.
parts.prob: 20 m squares smooth out narrow ditches and road edges.

parts.d: NLCD 2021: what covers the ground and how much of it is paved.
parts.done: Pavement share and surface roughness on every square.
parts.left: Nothing planned.
parts.prob: None open.

parts.d: USDA soils and land cover give how much rain runs off (NRCS curve number).
parts.done: Curve numbers on every square, with one calibration factor.
parts.left: Tie runoff to how wet the ground is before each storm.
parts.prob: One calibration factor is used for every storm.

parts.d: How wet or frozen the ground is before the storm.
parts.done: Dry, soaked and frozen ground can be set for what-if runs.
parts.left: A daily soil-moisture feed for live forecasts.
parts.prob: No reliable daily soil-moisture source for the district yet.

parts.d: Where streams pass under roads, and how much water each culvert can pass.
parts.done: Streams carved to their normal depth; culvert sizes from NAACC surveys where they exist; blocked-culvert what-if runs.
parts.left: Sizes and condition for culverts with no survey.
parts.prob: Many culverts have no recorded size or condition.

parts.d: Street inlets and pipes that carry water in built-up areas.
parts.done: City inlet locations collected.
parts.left: Pipe sizes and a way to represent the network.
parts.prob: Pipe network data (sizes, depths, condition) are held by each city.

parts.d: Rising groundwater under roads and foundations.
parts.left: Choose the groundwater data and how it links to roads and foundations.
parts.prob: Groundwater observations near roads are sparse.

parts.d: LISFLOOD-FP 8.2 moves the water across every 20 m square, every second.
parts.done: Runs for past storms and for every live forecast on free cloud computers.
parts.left: Shorter run times.
parts.prob: A forecast takes a few hours from the weather model's issue time to the road list.

parts.d: Water depth read every 10 m along every road; about 30 cm means likely closed.
parts.done: Depth along every road segment, counting only the water the storm added.
parts.left: Better handling of bridges and roads beside streams.
parts.prob: Roads damaged when their edge washes out, without deep standing water, are missed.

parts.d: Washouts and edge erosion along roads and at crossings.
parts.done: Water speed and depth beside every road are recorded.
parts.left: A damage rule built and checked on more storms.
parts.prob: Detailed damage records exist for one storm only.

parts.d: People who can no longer reach a hospital, fire station or police station in time.
parts.done: Road network, detours and access to hospitals, fire and police for every storm run.
parts.left: Network-level measures of delay; a check against real response records.
parts.prob: No recorded emergency response times to check against.

parts.d: Before a storm, the roads most likely to close, updated every hour.
parts.done: Automatic forecasts when heavy rain is coming; roads listed as likely or possible.
parts.left: Automatic scoring of every forecast after the storm.
parts.prob: Its quality depends on the forecast rain.

parts.t: Chance of closure as a percentage
parts.d: A calibrated probability for each road, instead of "k of 8".
parts.done: Roads are ordered by their chance of flooding.
parts.left: Show it as a percentage once it is proven.
parts.prob: Needs more storms with reported closures to calibrate.

parts.d: Which culverts would close roads first if they were blocked.
parts.done: A ranked list from what-if runs on one storm.
parts.left: Confirm the list with culvert condition data.
parts.prob: Culvert condition data are needed to confirm it.

parts.d: The same storm with more rain, wetter or frozen ground, or blocked culverts.
parts.done: Public what-if runs for one storm.
parts.left: More storms.
parts.prob: Only one storm so far.

parts.d: A learned copy of the flood engine for fast, district-wide forecasts.
parts.left: Start after the physics model is validated.
parts.prob: Waits on the physics model.

parts.d: Road closures and damage from news, agencies, cities and the public, never used as inputs.
parts.done: Reports gathered and matched to roads for past storms in central and eastern Massachusetts.
parts.left: Official damage inventories for more storms.
parts.prob: Reports cluster where people live and drive, and official records are few.

parts.d: Every live forecast is recorded and checked after the storm.
parts.done: Running since 3 Nov 2026.
parts.left: More storms.
parts.prob: Few storms so far this season.

parts.d: The map, this page and the explanation of the model.
parts.done: Live map, replays, what-if explorer and forecast view.
parts.left: The 3D explanation and this progress page.
parts.prob: None open.
